scope: accepted=true questions in wave2-acceptance-2026-10-14.json for biology__b3 (20 of 20). All 20 were accepted.

verdicts.why: Key D is the only correct statement: restriction enzymes recognise palindromic sites and cut within them. A (random cuts), B (eukaryotic origin) and C (ligase's job) are clearly wrong.
BamHI lies inside the tet gene of pBR322, so insertion inactivates tetracycline resistance and leaves ampicillin resistance intact. Key C follows directly.
Two cuts open a circular molecule into two fragments regardless of size. Distractors 3 (linear count), 4 (strand count) and 1 are each explained.
Matching is unambiguous: restriction endonuclease-III, ligase-I, Taq-II, lysozyme-IV. Key B is the only option with all four pairs correct.
Isolation, then ligation into vector, transformation and selection is the standard cloning order. Only key C preserves it.

Correct key D was markedly longer and more detailed than the three distractors, which is a length cue. Repair: shortened D to 'The alkaline midgut dissolves the crystals and gut proteases cleave the protoxin' (same meaning, key unchanged). Protoxin activation in the alkaline midgut is the NCERT point.

Key A was the longest option (19 words against 15 to 17). Repair: removed 'own' from A so its length is closer to the others. Key A (siRNA-mediated silencing of the nematode's own genes after dsRNA uptake) is unchanged and still uniquely correct.

Golden rice (beta-carotene), Flavr Savr (delayed ripening), Rosie (human alpha-lactalbumin milk) and Bt cotton (Cry protein) each map to exactly one List II item. Key B is the only correct combination.
Ex vivo ADA therapy runs isolate, culture, transduce with retroviral vector, then infuse. Only key B gives that order.
A (insulin chains combined) and C (ex vivo gene therapy) are true. B (Cry protoxins) and D (Golden rice is beta-carotene, not iron) are false. Key C is the only option matching exactly A and C.
Gause's Paramecium competition experiment with a shared limited food supply is the classic competitive exclusion case. The other three options are unrelated rules.

Key D was the longest option, and the 'lion and a deer' distractor was very short. Repair: C changed to 'A lion and the deer it hunts' and D shortened to 'A lichen fungus and the alga in its thallus'. Lichen remains the only mutualism pair and key D is unchanged.

The explanation accounted for 100, 120 and the correct 80 but not 20, which is what results from using N/K in place of (1 - N/K). Repair: added that explanation. The key 80 is verified: 0.5 x 200 x 0.8.
Exponential per capita rate is constant (A true). Logistic per capita rate falls with N (B false). dN/dt is zero at K (C true). Growth rate peaks at K/2, not K (D false). Key C is correct.
NPP = GPP minus producer respiration gives 800 - 300 = 500. The distractors 300, 800 and 1100 each reflect a specific wrong operation and are explained.
Ten percent transfer applied three times from 10,000 kJ gives 10 kJ at the tertiary level. The distractors 100, 1000 and 1 correspond to stopping early or adding one transfer too many.
Xerarch succession on bare rock runs lichen, moss, herb, shrub, which is the NCERT order. Key C is the only option with this order.
The evil quartet is habitat loss, overexploitation, alien species and co-extinction. Sacred groves are a conservation measure, so B is the correct NOT option.
Seed bank is the only ex situ option. Biosphere reserve, national park and wildlife sanctuary are all in situ. The four options are balanced in length.

Water hyacinth forms floating mats (III), Lantana is an invasive shrub (IV), Parthenium causes allergy and dermatitis (II), and the African catfish threatens native fish (I). Key D is the only correct set.
